name: gathering kindred rooms together
old_label: gathering kindred rooms in a hub sub
gloss: Kindred rooms (a league's teams, a region's subs, sister fandoms) gather their canvas work in one hub sub or chat.
must_show: A hub for many kindred rooms used or proposed: 'everyone go to r/CFBplace', a regional place sub for several teams, one chat for a league, members sent to the hub for help.
must_not_show: A separate sub for one room's own work (T3-090); one joint mark made by two rooms (T3-056); calls for hands sent to kindred subs (T3-062).
decide_when_both: A hub that also makes a joint mark: T3-013 for the hub, T3-056 added when the joint mark has concepts of its own.

discriminators.question: Is the new sub for this room's own work (T3-090), or a hub for many kindred rooms (T3-013)?
Do two or more rooms make one mark together (T3-056), or gather their separate works in a hub (T3-013)?
Are kindred subs asked for hands for this room (T3-062), or gathered into a common hub (T3-013)?

varies: From a college football place sub to a regional hub for a city's teams and a European chat server.
is_not: A room opening its own canvas sub (T3-090).
two_or_half: It could be half of T3-090, a sub for the canvas; kept apart because the hub belongs to many rooms.

exemplars.quote: #EVERYONE GO TO /r/CFBPLACE FOR THIS SORTA STUFF.
i asked for help in r/nbaplace
Come discuss it over at /r/716Place

name: tallying kindred rooms' works
old_label: tallying kindred rooms' works on the canvas
gloss: Members count which kindred rooms (teams, schools, bands) made it onto the canvas and which were lost.
must_show: An inventory of kindred rooms' marks on the canvas: which teams, schools or subs made it, which were covered, where they are.
must_not_show: Decoding the finished picture in general (T3-018); remarking on the pictures beside the room's own mark (T3-052).
decide_when_both: A tally inside a reading of the final canvas: T3-018 when the whole picture is read, T3-019 when the kindred rooms are counted.

discriminators.question: Is the whole finished picture decoded (T3-018), or the kindred rooms' marks counted (T3-019)?
Are pictures beside the mark remarked on (T3-052), or kindred rooms' marks across the canvas tallied (T3-019)?

varies: From a guess that only two NBA teams made it to a list of hockey logos kept or covered.
is_not: Explaining what each picture on the finished canvas is (T3-018).
two_or_half: It is thin and could be half of T3-018; kept apart because the count is of the room's own kind of community.

exemplars.quote: Nucks made it, Wings recreated a smaller version of theirs.
I believe that us and the Lakers are the only NBA teams with our logo on there.
The bottom left corner seems to have a few

name: making joint marks with others
old_label: making a joint mark with kindred rooms
gloss: Two or more rooms make one mark together: a shared design, a combined flag, lettering finished for each other.
must_show: A mark designed or built jointly by two or more rooms: shared borders made into a design, flags combined, each finishing part of the other's work, a joint emblem.
must_not_show: Help sent to another room's own work (T3-011); a member adding a personal piece to a shared mark (T3-060); national flags joined by a heart (T3-079).
decide_when_both: A joint mark of two national flags joined by a heart: T3-079; any other joint mark: T3-056.

discriminators.question: Is help sent to another's own work (T3-011), or one mark made together (T3-056)?
Are national flags joined with a heart (T3-079), or another joint mark made (T3-056)?
Do rooms ally for defence or a fight (T3-150), or make one mark together (T3-056)?
Is one mark made jointly by rooms (T3-056), or a personal piece added to it (T3-060)?
Do two or more rooms make one mark together (T3-056), or gather their separate works in a hub (T3-013)?
Do the rooms make one mark together (T3-056), or keep two rival marks side by side (T3-025)?

varies: From a beanie and lettering traded between two fandoms to ANZAC flags built together before the Americans woke.
is_not: Sending pixels to a neighbour's defence (T3-011).
two_or_half: With T3-079 it is one kind, the joint mark; they stay two because hearts between national flags are a distinct and common form.

exemplars.quote: They're finishing our beanie and we're finishing their lettering.
a row of heart-faced avocados wherever we meet up, and we maintain a strong border together
We are working together now on making a second flag to the left side.

name: hailing the colour corners
gloss: Members of other subs cheer the colour corners and factions, or call people to their side.
must_show: Outsiders hailing or cheering a colour faction or corner, or calling others to its side, without being its own members.
must_not_show: A faction's own members professing loyalty (T3-174); spreading the colour (T3-171).
decide_when_both: A member of another sub who joins the faction and hails it: T3-163 for the joining, T3-096 for the hailing.

discriminators.question: Do the faction's own members profess loyalty (T3-174), or do other subs' members cheer it (T3-096)?
Is the colour spread on the canvas (T3-171), or cheered in talk (T3-096)?
Does a member defect to the faction (T3-163), or only cheer it (T3-096)?

varies: From 'all hail blue corner' in a game sub to a streamer's sub calling its army to the purple side.
is_not: The Blue Corner's own members hailing their empire (T3-174).
two_or_half: It is half of T3-174, loyalty to a colour, voiced by outsiders; kept apart because the cheering room is not the faction.

exemplars.quote: ALL HAIL BLUE CORNER
ALL HAIL BLUE CORNER!
Join us in our honorable fight against the blue scum!

name: defecting from a rival faction
gloss: Members announce that they have left a rival faction and joined this one.
must_show: Defection or conversion between canvas factions: 'defector from the Blue Corner', 'converting from the Void', joining the lattice's army with a first pixel.
must_not_show: A faction splitting over doctrine (T3-190); outsiders cheering a faction (T3-096).
decide_when_both: A member leaving over doctrine to found or join a splinter: T3-190 when the split is the doing, T3-163 when the member's crossing is.

discriminators.question: Does a faction split over doctrine (T3-190), or does a member cross from a rival faction (T3-163)?
Does a member cross over (T3-163), or only cheer a faction (T3-096)?
Is loyalty professed by members (T3-174), or a member's crossing announced (T3-163)?

varies: From one defector's title post to convert stories told in a faction's thread.
is_not: A faction splitting into rival doctrines (T3-190).
two_or_half: It could be half of T3-174, loyalty declared; kept apart because the declaration renounces another faction.

exemplars.quote: I'm converting from r/TheBlueCorner
Defector from the Blue Corner
Defector from The Void

name: spreading a faction's colour
old_label: spreading a colour over the canvas
gloss: A colour faction spreads its colour across the canvas: expanding the corner, covering others with its colour, tendrils and cores.
must_show: A colour, not a picture, spread as the faction's aim: calls to expand the corner, to cover the canvas in the colour, to grow tendrils, the colour treated as territory.
must_not_show: A room's picture extended into a neighbour's space (T3-061); a rival's work defaced (T3-006); loyalty to the faction professed in talk (T3-174).
decide_when_both: Spreading the colour over a rival's work: T3-171 when the colour's spread is the aim, T3-006 or T3-061 when the target is.

discriminators.question: Is a picture grown into a neighbour's space (T3-061), or a colour spread as the aim (T3-171)?
Is a rival's work destroyed (T3-006), or the faction's colour spread over whatever lies in its way (T3-171)?
Is the colour spread on the canvas (T3-171), or loyalty to it professed (T3-174)?
Is the room's work extended (T3-041), or a colour spread for its own sake (T3-171)?
Is the colour spread on the canvas (T3-171), or cheered in talk (T3-096)?

varies: From a corner that grows a few rows to a Void meant to consume the whole canvas; red spread as a political colour.
is_not: A room extending its logo into a neighbour's space (T3-061).
two_or_half: It could be half of T3-061, taking space; kept apart because the colour itself is the work.

exemplars.quote: We shall spread the purple monarchy all over the canvas and defeat the blue usurpers!
TWO TEAMS: ONE TO RID THE VOID OF ALL MATTER, ONE TO EXPAND OUR CANCER TO THE ENTIRE PLACE.
Start expanding the green corner!

name: renewing the order's oaths
gloss: A canvas-born order lays down or renews its rules, oaths and membership.
must_show: An order's or faction's own rules, commandments, oaths or membership rolls set or renewed: commandments for its members, a yearly renewal, officers appointed by the order.
must_not_show: Elections for office (T3-173); one member put in charge of the work (T3-101).
decide_when_both: Officers appointed under the order's rules: T3-172; officers voted in: T3-173.

discriminators.question: Are offices filled by election (T3-173), or the order's rules and oaths laid down or renewed (T3-172)?
Is a leader named for the work (T3-101), or the order's standing rules set (T3-172)?

varies: From commandments for a purple faction to an order of knights meeting once a year.
is_not: A faction voting in a new leader (T3-173).
two_or_half: With T3-173 it is one kind, a faction governing itself; they stay two because an election is a different act from laying down rules.

exemplars.quote: 1. Respect thy fellow Purple. 2. Spare the art, for it is beautiful. 3. Consume all blue.
we picked up some new members and we picked up some old members.
Basically we meet up once a year to shitpost with each other.

name: holding elections for office
gloss: A canvas-born faction holds elections for its leaders and offices.
must_show: Elections in a faction: a new leader elected, voter registration, a round of elections, objections to holding them.
must_not_show: Votes on the work (T3-066); one member put in charge with no vote (T3-101).
decide_when_both: A leader elected who then puts choices to polls: T3-173 for the election, T3-066 for the polls.

discriminators.question: Is a choice about the work voted (T3-066), or a person elected to office (T3-173)?
Is a leader named with no vote (T3-101), or elected (T3-173)?
Are rules and oaths laid down (T3-172), or offices filled by vote (T3-173)?

varies: From an election held during an attack to voter registration after the event.
is_not: A poll on whether to fight, expand or move (T3-066).

exemplars.quote: Election for new leader!
With the April Fools Event over it is time to begin the election progress.
YOUR HAVING FUCKING ELECTIONS WHILE WE'RE GETTING ATTACKED

name: professing loyalty to a colour
old_label: professing loyalty to a colour faction
gloss: A colour faction's members profess loyalty to it: hails, slogans, propaganda, the colour as faith or empire.
must_show: Members of a colour faction professing its cause: 'all hail the Bluempire', 'hail the all-consuming Void', the colour cast as faith, empire or calling, propaganda praised.
must_not_show: Other subs' members cheering the faction (T3-096); spreading the colour on the canvas (T3-171).
decide_when_both: Hails that call members to spread the colour: T3-171 when the spreading is called, T3-174 when loyalty is the point (rule 0 lines pair T3-174 with T3-031 and T3-171).

discriminators.question: Do the faction's own members profess loyalty (T3-174), or other subs' members cheer it (T3-096)?
Is loyalty professed (T3-174), or the colour spread (T3-171)?
Is the joke the faction's colour cult (T3-174), or any running in-joke of the room (T3-031)?
Is loyalty professed to a colour faction (T3-174), or an alliance made between rooms (T3-150)?
Is loyalty professed by members (T3-174), or a member's crossing announced (T3-163)?

varies: From a one-line hail to the Void cast as a calling and a fit; propaganda posters.
is_not: A game sub hailing the Blue Corner from outside (T3-096).
two_or_half: See T3-096: loyalty to a colour, kept two by whether the speaker belongs.

exemplars.quote: ALL HAIL THE BLUEMPIRE!!
Hail The All Consuming Void!
10/10 propaganda. would vote for purple again

name: splitting a faction over doctrine
gloss: A canvas faction splits over what it stands for: pure colour or art, erasing or cleaning, the void or coexistence.
must_show: Dispute over a faction's doctrine that divides it: members leaving for a purer version, splinter subs founded, the faction's past and true nature argued.
must_not_show: A member defecting from a rival faction (T3-163); a member quitting under strain (T3-181).
decide_when_both: A member leaving over doctrine: T3-190 when the split in the faction is the doing, T3-163 when the crossing to another faction is.

discriminators.question: Does a member cross from a rival faction (T3-163), or does the faction split over its doctrine (T3-190)?
Does a member quit under strain (T3-181), or over the faction's doctrine (T3-190)?
Is a political ideology argued from the canvas (T3-179), or a faction's own canvas doctrine (T3-190)?

varies: From one eraser leaving for the black to a colour faction arguing whether it was once the void.
is_not: A member giving up because the work became stressful (T3-181).
two_or_half: It could be half of T3-174, doctrine professed, turned to dispute; kept apart because the faction divides.

exemplars.quote: Henceforth, going to begin spreading the black, as they are more true to the ideology I was seeking.
